INTRODUCTIONM
RC parallel circuits consist of resistors and capacitors connected in parallel.
In this circuit, closing S1 places R1 and R2 in parallel to C3, C4 and R4.
S4 and S5 allow one or both capacitors to be placed in the circuit.
S6 places the capacitive branch in parallel to R1 and R2 forming an RC parallel circuit.
R4 is a sampling resistor used to measure current in the capacitive branch of the parallel circuit.
In this lesson, the phase angle between Ir and Ic is measured and the following relationship is proven.
Let's begin the lesson on RC PARALLEL CIRCUIT OPERATION...................

6. Change the frequency on the function generator. Notice, the phase difference changes. You are changing the value of Xc which changes Ic. When Ic changes, total current also changes....
A higher frequency than 20 kHz decreases Xc. The capacitive branch starts to become pure resistive and the phase difference between the two branches in the parallel circuit approaches 0 degrees.

5. Place CH2 probe to TP6. Use TP1 as oscilloscope ground. Notice the zero crossing points on the oscilloscope display. This indicates the overall phase difference in the circuit.
6. Change the frequency on the function generator. Notice, the phase difference changes. You are changing the value of Xc which changes Ic. When Ic changes, total current also changes.
A higher frequency than 20 kHz decreases Xc. The capacitive branch starts to become pure resistive and the phase difference between the two branches in the parallel circuit approaches 0 degrees.
Frequencies below 20 kHz increase Xc. The capacitive branch comes closer to pure capacitive. The phase difference between the two branches in the parallel circuit approaches 90 degrees.
7. Return the function generator frequency to 20 kHz.
8. Set S4 DOWN on PC130-12. Notice, the phase difference increased. Capacitance decreased which increased Xc.
9. Increase R4 to maximum resistance. Notice, the phase difference approaches 0 degrees. The capacitive branch becomes almost all resistive.
10. Decrease R4 to minimum resistance. The phase difference approaches 90 degrees. The capacitive branch becomes almost all capacitive.
